item.title: At His First Show In Georgia, Moby Talks About ‘Music’s Ability to Reach Everybody – And to Reach Them In the Most Personal Way’
item.description:
Here's a short and engaging podcast script based on the article:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to "Trending on Billboard". I'm your host, and today we're talking about legendary electronic music artist, Moby. He recently took the stage in Georgia for the first time as part of his 2026 global tour. We had the chance to sit down with him backstage and talk about music, activism, and more.
[Soft music transition]
Host: Moby, thanks for taking the time to chat with us. You're performing in Georgia for the first time. What are your thoughts on the country and the audience?
Moby: I've only been here for a couple of days, and I'm really fascinated by Georgia. Tbilisi feels like a European city, even though it's a thousand miles away from Europe. I like it, yet I don't fully understand it, and that's what makes it so fascinating.
Host: That's really interesting. With your long journey in the music industry, what do you think is the biggest illusion that the industry creates for emerging artists?
Moby: I think one of the biggest illusions is when you're young and successful, everybody's nice to you. But that doesn't always last. When you're old and not successful, they might not be as nice. It's just the nature of things.
Host: That's a valuable insight. Let's talk about your activism. You're a well-known advocate for animal rights. What do you think is the main shift in the human mindset that's necessary for people to understand the importance of animal rights?
Moby: I think it's the ability to act logically and in accordance with our beliefs. If we like animals and don't want to hurt or kill them, the logical action would be to not eat them, to not pay someone else to hurt or kill them. It's about being consistent with our values.
[Soft music transition]
Host: Thanks, Moby, for sharing your thoughts with us today. It's clear that you're not only a talented musician but also a passionate advocate for important causes.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today's episode of "Trending on Billboard". Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you next time!
